name: Biak Hooded Pitta
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: Beautiful leaf-green pitta of Biak Island, off northwestern New Guinea. Like the other “Hooded-type” pittas with which it was formerly grouped, this species has a black head, powder-blue shoulder patch, and red on the lower belly and undertail.

name: Bernier's Vanga
rangeDescription: Humid forest of eastern madagascar
description: Large, slim, dark, long-billed vanga. Males are glossy black, females are rich brown with dark bars, and both sexes show a piercing pale eye.

name: White-eared Jacamar
rangeDescription: Colombia east of the andes to northeastern peru and western amazonian brazil
description: Chunky-looking bird with a small head and a larger bill than other jacamars, recalling a kingfisher. Chestnut-colored overall with a pinkish-red bill.

name: Marbled Murrelet
rangeDescription: Western aleutian islands and alaska to central california
description: Small seabird that breeds in old-growth evergreen forests, sometimes far from the coast. Often in small flocks on coastal waters, where it dives underwater searching for fish.

name: Fairy Pitta
rangeDescription: Southern japan to korea and southeastern china; winters to southeastern asia and borneo
description: A beautiful ground-dweller of well-shaded forests. Adult mostly green above, creamy tan below, with vivid red patch in undertail and central belly and multicolored head, with black mask, tan eyebrow, white throat, and rufous-and-black crown.

name: Numfor Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Numfor (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A small dull-colored warbler with an indistinct pale eyebrow, a dull greenish upperside, a pale throat, and dull yellowish underparts. Usually shows an indistinct wingbar.

name: Zebra Dove
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar through the thai-malay peninsula to sumatra, java, and lombok; also philippines (native or introduced?), and many feral populations, e.g. the seychelles, mascarenes, indochina, borneo, hawaii, and tahiti, among others
description: A small, grayish brown dove with dark bars on the breast and back, and bare blue skin around the eye. The call is a rapid series of short “coos,” higher pitched and faster than Spotted Dove.

name: Long-bearded Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Alpine grassland of east-central new guinea
description: A long, slender honeyeater of subalpine forest and shrubland in eastern New Guinea. All sooty gray-black plumage with long tail and very long, thin, curved bill, long white, whispy beard from the base of the bill, and a yellow-orange wattle at the back of the eye.

name: White-throated Pewee
rangeDescription: Suriname to french guiana and far northeastern brazil (amapá)
description: Small, inconspicuous, locally-distributed flycatcher. Both sexes are entirely dark gray with exception of prominent white throat patch.

name: Little Gray Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Sahel (southwestern mauritania to senegambia, chad, and west-central sudan)
description: Small, pale woodpecker of the Sahel. The back is pale gray with white barring, the rump is red, the underparts are heavily spotted and barred, and there is a gray mark on the cheek.

name: Roberts's Warbler
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern zimbabwe and adjacent southwestern mozambique
description: A dull gray-brown prinia-like warbler with a long and graduated tail, pale gray throat, ochre eyes, and pinkish legs. Pairs and family groups may join mixed-species flocks, foraging studiously through the lower branches of forest, undergrowth and bracken, forest edge, and occasionally pausing to chatter in unison.

name: Sri Lanka Woodshrike
rangeDescription: Sri lanka
description: Small gray songbird with heavy bill, dark mask, and white eyebrow. Underparts pale whitish; in flight note white rump.

name: Red-bellied Myzomela
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: A bulky, striking myzomela, mostly pitch black with a bright red rump and a bright crimson chest, throat, and flanks forming a “vest.” Belly, back, and head deep black. Female chocolate-brown above and ruddy-brown below.

name: African Crake
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: Chunky, mid-sized rail. Note the black-and-brown scalloped back, gray head and chest, barred belly, reddish bill and yellowish legs.

name: Mountain Thornbill
rangeDescription: Rainforest of northeastern queensland (cooktown to paluma range)
description: Small bird with thin pointed bill found in middle- to high-elevation rainforests in far northern Queensland. Greenish gray above, pale below, with faint streaks on chest, pale eye, and faint pale speckling on gray forecrown.

name: Wandering Tattler
rangeDescription: Siberia and alaska; winters to northern south america, hawaii, and southwestern oceania
description: Medium-sized, gray shorebird with short yellow legs and straight bill. Elongated, horizontal posture.

name: Yellow-crowned Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (montane forest of luzon)
description: A tiny bird of mossy montane forest and edge on Luzon. Male has glossy black upperparts, pale underparts (whiter on the throat), and the namesake yellow crown stripe.

name: Mountain Plover
rangeDescription: Great plains of western canada to southwestern usa; winters to northern mexico
description: Medium-sized, plain buffy plover that favors flat open areas with little or no vegetation. Plain whitish underparts with no breast band.

name: Maguari Stork
rangeDescription: Plains and marshes of west-central south america east of the andes
description: Unmistakable species given its size, very long bill, and red legs. Its black flight feathers and tail contrast with its largely white body, resembling European White Stork.

name: Senegal Batis
rangeDescription: Senegambia to southern mauritania, southern niger, and cameroon
description: Typical black, white, and dark-gray batis. Note the chest band, which is black in males and rufous in females.
